headline: High: Botpress can feed untrusted content into Kestra workflows, creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-action risk; Kestra’s broad write/network privileges amplify impact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support agent that can ingest external conversation content, while Kestra can execute workflows from stdin/stdout, files, and many APIs. That creates a plausible default pathway where Botpress-produced text is treated as instructions by Kestra or a downstream task. No provenance or isolation is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Botpress output is passed into a Kestra task without provenance tagging
IF Kestra parses Botpress-generated text as workflow instructions or parameters
mitigations: Add an explicit allowlist parser for Botpress-to-Kestra handoff
Insert a human review step before Kestra executes Botpress-derived content
Tag Botpress outputs as untrusted and reject instruction-like tokens
Use a separate queue or file namespace for handoff data
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata enforcement between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Botpress has no documented egress, but Kestra has broad network egress and reads/writes files in /app/storage and /tmp. If shared workspace data from Botpress reaches Kestra, Kestra can transmit it to third-party services or logs. The pairwise leak path is plausible in default orchestration, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Botpress artifacts or conversation data are stored in a Kestra-readable path
IF Kestra tasks forward those files or variables to HTTP, Slack, email, or cloud APIs
mitigations: Keep Botpress and Kestra on separate volumes
Disable or restrict Kestra tasks that export data externally
Redact secrets before writing shared artifacts
Review Kestra logs for Botpress-originated payloads
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, and Kestra can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Even without a shared lock, overlapping mutation of shared files or environments can cause conflicts. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this is medium rather than high, but the write surface is real on Kestra and package mutation is real on Botpress.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or environment
IF Botpress package installation and Kestra task execution occur concurrently
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Pin package versions for Botpress jobs
Run Kestra tasks in isolated containers
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration system with email, Slack, PagerDuty, cloud, and shell actions, so if it consumes Botpress output as authoritative, a bad Botpress answer can trigger real downstream actions. Botpress is a support chatbot, not a verified planner, and no verification step is documented. That makes the cascade dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Botpress output to populate workflow variables or task parameters
IF those variables drive notifications, deployments, or shell commands without validation
mitigations: Require schema validation on Botpress outputs
Add a manual approval gate before action tasks
Limit Kestra tasks to read-only dry runs first
Log and diff Botpress-derived parameters before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between Botpress and Kestra

E_compliance.rationale: Botpress is a customer-support system and Kestra touches logs, messages, notifications, database data, and cloud storage data. If support content includes regulated or personal data and is handed into Kestra workflows, retention and residency controls can diverge. The profiles do not show certifications or residency guarantees, so the safest supported rating is medium.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts contain personal or regulated data
IF Kestra stores, logs, or forwards that data under different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify support data before workflow ingestion
Mask personal data in Botpress outputs
Set shorter retention on Kestra logs and artifacts
Restrict exports to approved regions
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements
